purpose: The manifest's eighteen security invariants, and the permanent record of which are ENFORCED by a named test and which are PENDING a subsystem that does not exist yet. A test asserting that a nonexistent system cannot be attacked passes forever and reads exactly like proof; this file is what stops that being invisible.
rules: An enforced invariant must name at least one test, and the suite proves that name resolves.
A pending invariant must name its missing subject and the phase expected to build it, and must have no test.
The pending count may fall without ceremony. It cannot rise without editing this file.
No invariant may be removed. The manifest's list is the list.
An invariant closed against a primitive with no production caller must say so in enforcedScope, and must carry a structural rule that fails if a caller appears which bypasses it.

invariants.manifestText: wrong devices cannot execute targeted jobs
invariants.enforcedBy: orion/core/jobs/queue.py start() checks the answering device against target_device. Added BY this suite: start authenticated the token and never asked who was answering.
orion/security/rules.py sensitive_actions_are_signed; binds on crossing a device boundary at R4+
orion/security/signing.py canonical_bytes over every field that can change the outcome
orion/security/rules.py external_data_does_not_drive_action; orion/core/context/domains.py classify() defaults to EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED

orion/security/request.py strict decoding; orion/security/risk.py derives risk and only DENIES on a declared mismatch

invariants.manifestText: deleted connections cannot continue refreshing tokens
invariants.enforcedBy: backend/vault/credentials.py: delete_connection revokes every credential under the connection in the same call rather than through a job or an event, because anything asynchronous leaves a window in which a deleted connection can still refresh. A revoked credential cannot be borrowed, and a deleted connection cannot be given a new one.
invariants.enforcedScope: The vault's own lifecycle, in memory. No OAuth provider is connected and nothing refreshes a real token yet, so what is proven is that the vault refuses -- not that a live refresh loop asks it. The cipher is injected: the production default raises rather than encrypting, so a deployment that forgets to configure one cannot store a credential at all.

invariants.manifestText: health data cannot leak into unrelated contexts
invariants.enforcedBy: orion/core/context/policy.py default-deny domain matrix; orion/core/eventbus/coupling.py cascade matrix

invariants.manifestText: email data cannot leak into unrelated contexts
client-provided user ownership fields cannot override server ownership
invariants.enforcedBy: orion/security/request.py has no trust field; orion/security/devices.py owns() answers from the directory

invariants.manifestText: one user cannot access another user's data
invariants.enforcedBy: backend/ownership.py: an Owner can only be made from an authenticated Session, and Repository has no method that does not take one first. Phase 8 additionally scopes idempotency keys per user.
invariants.enforcedScope: The ownership RESOLUTION layer, with an in-memory store. No database exists yet: Phase 11 must subclass Repository rather than query around it. Enforced structurally rather than by convention -- an Owner can only be built by resolve_owner (a private construction proof), every Repository method takes an owner first (owner_first_violations asserts it), and records are keyed per owner so another user gets the same answer for your record as for one that does not exist.

invariants.manifestText: arbitrary internal URLs cannot be fetched through SSRF
invariants.enforcedBy: backend/egress.py: default-deny host allowlist, https only on 443, no credentials in the URL, and refusal of loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, reserved and cloud-metadata addresses in both literal and hostname form, including IPv4-mapped IPv6.
invariants.enforcedScope: The URL, and only the URL. THREE things are not covered and must not be read as if they were: (1) nothing in ORION fetches a URL yet, so this guard has no production caller -- it is enforced at the only door that will exist, not at a door in use; (2) redirects must be re-checked hop by hop, because a permitted host can answer with a 302 to a forbidden one; (3) the HTTP client must pin the resolved address and connect to Target.host rather than the URL string, because DNS can answer differently between the check and the connection. Point (1) is why backend/boundaries.py additionally forbids every backend file except egress.py from importing an HTTP client: a future fetch that skips the guard fails the boundary check instead of reopening this invariant silently.
